findings.description: SYS-SUP-033 requires the latch, per-code counts and fault history to survive software and watchdog resets. SYE-SUP-067 uses the microcontroller as a placeholder; no reset-retentive storage element or its reset and power-loss behavior is established.
findings.requested_change: Identify the retained storage and allocate the required retention and clearing behavior to it.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-015 requires fault-free start-up without a watchdog reset. Watchdog activation, first-refresh timing and integrity-check duration remain unresolved, so the start-up sequence cannot establish that outcome.
findings.requested_change: Establish watchdog activation and servicing during start-up and substantiate the integrity-check duration against the watchdog limits.

findings.description: DEC-SYE-006 reserves 5% of processor time for the run-time check and 5% for the remaining supervisor work. OP-SYE-007 records that CRC throughput and the other execution costs are unknown, so feasibility of SYS-SUP-022, SYS-SUP-052 and SYS-SUP-058 remains unshown.
findings.requested_change: Provide platform evidence and a budget analysis establishing the segment, full-pass and aggregate processor limits.

findings.description: DEC-SYE-007 identifies shared-processor, memory and peripheral interference cases, but relies on A-INT-1 and A-INT-2 to exclude faulty task accesses. OP-SYE-008 leaves their enforcement unresolved. An interface declaration alone does not establish that faulty application execution cannot corrupt supervision or refresh a watchdog.
findings.requested_change: Establish and justify enforceable isolation or other protections against the identified interference, and record any system-level decision that remains necessary.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-053 and SYS-SUP-054 require fault injection and verification without the real board. OP-SYE-004 records that the named environments' GPIO, serial and reset-flag observation and stimulation capabilities are not established.
findings.requested_change: Establish the required stimulation and observation mechanisms in the verification environments and their feasibility.
